cohort: 1,118 term (37-42 weeks gestation) antenatal women with singleton pregnancies, with 559 women with high-risk pregnancies as cases and 559 low-risk pregnant women as controls.
finding: Placental weight and birth weight were significantly lower in high-risk pregnancies compared to low-risk pregnancies, while the placental birth weight ratio was higher in high-risk cases, and placental weight was positively correlated with birth weight.
birth_weight: Varied, but significantly lower in the high-risk group (2.68 kg +/- 0.53 kg) compared to the low-risk group (2.88 kg +/- 0.4 kg).
